author: reek
body: The first runtime coverage the engine foreword has ever had. Until CL 7517 eighteen of its forty-two chapters could not type-check: the math foreword moved Vec3, Vec4, Quat and Mat4 to Real and everything built on them stayed fixed-point. They compile now, and compiling is not the same as working. A frustum plane with the wrong sign culls the whole scene in silence; a projection that has lost its perspective divide draws a flat card. Nothing about either shows up in a type.

author: reek
body: So this renders. Renderer3D walks the scene, projects, shades and fills every triangle in Codex, with no host GPU and no rasterizer port, and the pixels it produces are counted. The counts are what pin the arithmetic down.

author: reek
body: A box at the origin is inside the frustum and a box parked far behind the camera is outside. These planes are extracted from a Real Mat4; they were four Integers until the migration, and had the extraction kept its old fixed-point scaling both answers would agree and the renderer would draw nothing at all.

author: reek
body: Counting what the rasterizer actually wrote. A drawn pixel is any pixel that is not the background, so the tally goes to zero if the geometry is culled away, and changes if the projection moves.
